top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, one writer, one prize part) is the only substantive proposal on the slate, and I see no literary ground to prefer no award. On the common criteria, as I can assess them from public knowledge and not from independent reading, his voice is distinctive, and the dense, patterned prose of the Orbitor sequence (Blinding is its first part) and Solenoid shows large formal architecture and imaginative and intellectual depth built from memory, the body and dream. The major structures exist, so the oeuvre can be assessed as a whole. Attribution is clean, with one writer and one language. The citation should be prose-centred, with poetry named as foundation and not as the basis of the award. Open uncertainties remain: how much of the Romanian sentence-level density and rhythm survives translation, whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it, and how much weight the poetry can bear. These are doubts about evidence, not findings that the work falls short, and they do not justify P000. The unanimity of the opening rankings is not treated as evidence of merit.
